evals.prompt: Je veux réaliser un benchmark concurrentiel du marché de l'assurance emprunteur en France pour notre client Banque Solaris. Les acteurs à analyser sont : CNP Assurances, Cardif (BNP), SwissLife, Apicil, et Alan. On veut comparer leurs offres sur le segment B2C, emprunt immobilier. Je n'ai pas encore décidé des dimensions d'analyse.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs Phase 0 interactively: asks Q1-Q5 in sequence, proposes insurance-adapted dimensions (e.g., Garanties & exclusions, Conditions d'accès, Tarification, Expérience client/digital), confirms mission config. Then collects data per actor, produces 5 actor files in outputs/assurance-emprunteur-banque-solaris/actors/ + pricing-synthesis.md + exec-summary.md + benchmark.json
assertions: Phase 0 asks at least 3 clarifying questions via AskUserQuestion before starting analysis
Proposed dimensions are adapted to insurance market — NOT the default LMD dimensions
mission-config.json is created in outputs/ before analysis starts
At least 3 actor .md files produced in outputs/assurance-emprunteur-banque-solaris/actors/
benchmark.json is present and valid JSON
Each actor file has a Sources block with at least one citation
No price data presented without a source marker (URL, document, or [ESTIMATION]/[N/D])
Skill presents a dimension selection menu with at least 3 options (A/B/C or equivalent) during Q4
Skill includes a rationale block ('Pourquoi ces axes' or equivalent) explaining why the proposed dimensions fit the insurance market

evals.prompt: Lance un benchmark LMD France pour Velora. Acteurs : Carvio, Rentalis, Drivalis, Rouli. Véhicule de référence Peugeot 308 équivalente, durées 1/3/6/12 mois, 500 km/mois. Utilise les dimensions standard.
evals.expected_output: Skill confirms mission config quickly (most info provided), uses default 4 default dimensions with minor LMD adaptation, produces 4 actor files, pricing-synthesis.md with 4x4 table (4 actors x 4 durations), exec-summary.md with positioning table, benchmark.json
assertions: Skill presents a mission config summary and asks for confirmation before starting
Uses the 4 standard default dimensions (Offre/Conditions, Contenu, Cibles/TOV, Pricing)
pricing-synthesis.md contains a table with columns for 1m/3m/6m/12m
All 4 actors appear in the pricing table
exec-summary.md contains a positioning table with all 4 actors
benchmark.json pricing_matrix.data array has 4 entries (one per actor)
benchmark.json is valid JSON (python3 -c "import json; json.load(open(...))" succeeds)
Skill presents a dimension selection menu with at least 3 options (A/B/C or equivalent) during Q4
Skill includes a rationale block ('Pourquoi ces axes' or equivalent) explaining why the proposed dimensions fit the LMD market

evals.prompt: J'ai besoin d'un benchmark des solutions de téléphonie mobile B2B en France. Je veux comparer Novatel Pro, Kaptel Business, Orbitel Entreprises et Free Pro. Je veux comprendre les offres, les prix, les engagements et ce qui les différencie. Je n'ai pas encore réfléchi aux dimensions.
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies dimensions are undefined, uses Q4 to propose telecom B2B-specific dimensions (e.g., Offres & forfaits, Couverture & qualité réseau, Services B2B & gestion de flotte, Tarification & engagement), confirms with user, then proceeds with analysis of 4 actors
assertions: Skill uses AskUserQuestion to propose and confirm telecom-specific dimensions before collecting data
Proposed dimensions include at least one telecom-specific concept (coverage, fleet management, network quality, etc.)
Skill presents a dimension selection menu with at least 3 options (A/B/C or equivalent) during Q4
Skill includes a rationale sentence ('Pourquoi ces axes' or equivalent) explaining why the proposed dimensions fit the telecom B2B market
At least 2 actor .md files produced
Each actor file contains an INSIGHTS section with ✅ and ⚠️ markers
Sources are cited in each actor file
benchmark.json actors array contains at least 2 entries

evals.prompt: Je veux benchmarker le marché du coworking premium en France, notamment à Paris et Lyon. Je ne sais pas encore quels acteurs analyser — peux-tu me proposer une liste ? Le client s'appelle WeWork qui cherche à comprendre ses concurrents directs.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs Step 0.2b peer discovery: performs at least 2 WebSearches to identify market actors, produces a categorized list of 6+ actors, presents it to the user for validation, and waits for confirmation before proceeding to Phase 1.
assertions: Skill does NOT immediately start Phase 1 — it triggers Step 0.2b peer discovery first
At least 2 distinct WebSearch queries are issued to find coworking market actors
Output includes a categorized list of at least 6 actors with one-line descriptions
Actors are grouped by category (e.g., pure-players, flex office réseaux, grands groupes)
Skill asks for user validation of the actor list via AskUserQuestion before proceeding
mission-config.json is NOT created until after user confirms the actor list

evals.prompt: Benchmark concurrentiel du marché des mutuelles santé entreprise en France pour notre client Mutualis. Acteurs : AG2R La Mondiale, Harmonie Mutuelle, Apicil, Axa Santé. Je veux définir moi-même les axes d'analyse — je ne veux pas utiliser des dimensions standard.
evals.expected_output: Skill presents sector-matched dimension proposal (Santé au Travail sector), then correctly enters option D flow: iterates with the consultant to define custom dimensions, confirms the final custom dimension set via AskUserQuestion before proceeding, then runs analysis with the consultant-defined dimensions.
assertions: Skill proposes sector-specific dimensions (Santé au Travail / mutuelle) before entering custom flow
Skill correctly handles consultant's request to define own axes — does NOT lock the standard dimensions without asking
Skill iterates with consultant via AskUserQuestion to collect and confirm custom dimensions
Custom dimensions are confirmed before Phase 1 data collection begins
mission-config.json reflects the custom dimensions (not the default 4 dims)
At least 2 actor .md files produced using the custom dimensions
benchmark.json dimensions array reflects the custom (not default) dimension set

evals.prompt: Benchmark RSE du marché de la mode responsable en France pour notre client AMI Paris. Acteurs : Veja, Patagonia Europe, Sézane, Balzac Paris. Je veux comparer leur maturité RSE : matières, chaîne d'approvisionnement, social, gouvernance. Va jusqu'au scorecard.
evals.expected_output: Skill classifies nature=maturity and sector=sustainability from the market description, loads the sustainability search module and the maturity profile, uses the maturity dimension sub-fields, produces actor files with sourced quantified metrics and verbatim-backed certifications, then a scorecard scored on the applicable total (core + maturity sector sections), never penalised for absent offer sections.
assertions: mission-config.json contains benchmark_nature = "maturity" and sector = "sustainability"
A legacy config carrying benchmark_type = "rse" is still accepted and read as the same nature
Actor dimensions use the maturity sub-fields (maturity_level, key_metrics, certifications, commitments) — NOT description/content/targets_tov/pricing
validate_benchmark.py actor mode returns PASS with no warning about vehicle_catalog or optional_services
The scorecard header states benchmark_nature, sector, the applicable section list and the applicable total
No scorecard section is scored 0 because it does not apply to this nature — non-applicable sections are marked N/A and excluded from the denominator
The scorecard total is NOT out of 80 — the denominator reflects the applicable sections only
A run with complete data can reach a score_pct of 90% or above (convergence is reachable for this nature)
Every certification, label, or third-party attribution carries a verbatim quote, or is marked [INTERPRETATION]
No claim states that a third party audited a company when the source only describes a methodology review
Phase 7 decision is taken on score_pct, not on a raw point total

evals.prompt: Le benchmark LMD Velora dans outputs/lmd-france-velora/ est déjà produit, le scorecard sort à 78%. Améliore-le et relance le scoring.
evals.expected_output: Skill enters Phase 7: reads the existing scorecard, classifies each gap as corrigeable or structurel, corrects only the corrigeable ones, regenerates only the deliverables whose source data changed plus benchmark.json and the HTML, re-scores, and appends a percentage-based comparison with the previous iteration.
assertions: Skill reads the existing benchmark-scorecard.md before making any change
Each gap is explicitly classified corrigeable or structurel
Only corrigeable gaps are worked on — structural gaps are documented, not retried
A synthesis file whose source data did not change is NOT regenerated
benchmark.json is regenerated from the actor JSONs, and the HTML from benchmark.json
The new scorecard contains a comparison block expressed in percentage points, not raw points
Iteration count is tracked and the run stops at 3 iterations maximum
If the score does not improve after an iteration, the skill stops and tells the consultant the remaining gaps are structural
No unsourced figure is introduced or retained to raise a score

evals.prompt: Benchmark des offres de mobilité partagée B2B en Suisse pour notre client TransRail. Acteurs : Sharego, Alpaloc, Drivalis Suisse, Citymove. Je veux les prix mensuels, et des captures d'écran des pages tarifaires pour illustrer le comité.
evals.expected_output: Skill sets nature=offer, sector=mobilite, locale country=CH / currency=CHF / output_language=fr, builds the comparability contract, nominates capture targets per actor, runs one capture pass via scripts/capture.py, and inlines the captioned derivatives in the HTML report.
assertions: mission-config.json carries benchmark_nature = "offer" and a sector, not a benchmark_type
locale.country is CH and locale.currency is CHF — INSEE and EUR are NOT assumed
The comparability contract is stated and validated with the consultant before data collection
Actor subagents do NOT launch a browser: they emit capture_targets with intent, url and claim
The orchestrator runs scripts/capture.py once over a merged capture-plan.json, not once per actor
capture-manifest.json exists and every displayed screenshot has status ok
A blocked capture (captcha/WAF) is documented as a structural gap, not retried in a loop
The HTML report inlines the .web.jpg derivatives, never the full-resolution PNGs
Every screenshot displayed carries its source URL and capture date
Prices in CHF are detected as prices by the validator (no currency-specific blind spot)

evals.prompt: Je veux comparer la maturité data & IA de 4 assureurs français : AXA, Generali, MAIF, Groupama. Où en sont-ils, qui est en avance, et sur quoi ? Pas de comparaison de prix, c'est un état des lieux.
evals.expected_output: Skill classifies nature=maturity (not offer, despite the actors being commercial companies) and sector=assurance, loads the maturity profile, uses maturity sub-fields, produces maturity-synthesis.md instead of pricing-synthesis.md, and applies the SOCLE / ÉCART / TERRAIN D'AVANCE recommendation frame.
assertions: benchmark_nature is maturity — the skill does NOT default to offer because the actors sell products
Dimension sub-fields are maturity_level / key_metrics / certifications / commitments
No pricing-synthesis.md is produced; the comparison synthesis is named after the metric family
The recommendation uses SOCLE / ÉCART / TERRAIN D'AVANCE, not Standard / Singularité / Unicité
Every quantified indicator carries a year — an undated maturity figure is rejected
The scorecard applies the maturity sector sections and excludes the offer ones as N/A
comparables[] rows use metric=indicator with a period equal to the reference year
No commercial projection block (pricing_matrix, vehicle_catalog) is generated

evals.prompt: Compare les 4 principaux fournisseurs de bornes de recharge pour copropriétés en France. Je ne sais pas trop comment structurer, c'est un sujet nouveau pour nous.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognises the subject fits neither offer nor maturity cleanly, runs the generic profile explicitly, declares the comparable metrics in the comparability contract, and scores on core sections only.
assertions: The skill states explicitly that it is running the generic profile and why
Dimension sub-fields are description / evidence / implication
The comparability contract declares each metric with a unit before any figure is collected
A metric with no declared unit stays in prose and does NOT enter comparables[]
The scorecard header says generic and scores core sections only, with sector sections marked N/A
The skill does not invent sector scorecard sections at run time
